cues.en: interpretability.
cues.zh: 可解釋性影片中的第一支。

cues.zh: 它放在檢查各層的章節中，但互資訊與共變異數，是實用且通用的

cues.en: analysis methods that work for lots of different situations and many different features of the model, and not just layers per se.
cues.zh: 分析方法，適用於許多不同情境，以及模型的許多不同特徵，不只是層本身。

cues.en: So the purpose of this video is to introduce you to the formula and interpretation of mutual information,
cues.zh: 這支影片的目的，是介紹互資訊的公式與解讀方式，

cues.en: and I'll show you how to implement it using several different approaches in Python.

cues.en: So this video is not really about LX per se, but the methods that you will use in later videos.
cues.zh: 所以這支影片並不直接談 LLM 本身，而是介紹後續影片會用到的方法。

cues.en: Mutual information is based on a quantity called entropy.
cues.zh: 互資訊以一個叫作熵的量為基礎。

cues.en: So let me first introduce you to the math and interpretation of entropy.
cues.zh: 所以先介紹熵的數學與解讀方式，

cues.en: And then we can switch to discussing mutual information.
cues.zh: 再轉而討論互資訊。

cues.en: Actually the word entropy is used in several different contexts and it has several different meanings.
cues.zh: 其實熵這個字會出現在幾種不同脈絡，也有幾種不同意義。

cues.en: You might be familiar with the concept of entropy in physics and thermodynamics, where that term entropy
cues.zh: 你可能熟悉物理與熱力學中的熵，在那裡，熵

cues.en: refers to the fact that order tends to move towards disorder, and things that are neat and organized eventually become chaotic and disorganized.
cues.zh: 表示有序往往會走向無序，整齊有條理的事物，最終會變得混亂無章。

cues.en: Unfortunately, this interpretation of entropy leads to some very difficult existential thoughts about the universe.
cues.zh: 不幸的是，這種熵的解讀，會引出一些關於宇宙、相當難受的存在性思考。

cues.en: But don't worry.
cues.zh: 但別擔心。

cues.en: The way that we will use entropy here in data analysis is a different interpretation from Claude Shannon,
cues.zh: 這裡在資料分析中使用熵的方式，來自 Claude Shannon 的另一種解讀，

cues.en: and it is much more upbeat and happy than the Then the thermodynamics interpretation in the context of information theory.
cues.zh: 比熱力學的解讀樂觀、快樂得多。在資訊理論中，

cues.en: Entropy is a quantification of the amount of variability or unexpectedness.
cues.zh: 熵量化的是變異程度或不可預期性，

cues.en: It's also usually called surprise in this literature.
cues.zh: 文獻中通常也稱為驚奇，

cues.en: In a data set.
cues.zh: 也就是資料集中的驚奇程度。

cues.en: So this graph over here shows entropy on the y axis and the probability of an event occurring on the x axis.
cues.zh: 這張圖的 y 軸是熵，x 軸是某事件發生的機率。

cues.en: Now when the probabilities are close to zero or close to one, then there isn't much unexpectedness happening.
cues.zh: 當機率接近零或接近一時，不可預期性就不高。

cues.en: For example, if we think about the probability of the sun coming up in the morning, that's a very high probability.
cues.zh: 例如想想早晨太陽升起的機率，那個機率非常高。

cues.en: Therefore, you are not surprised when the sun comes up in the morning.
cues.zh: 因此早上太陽升起時，你不會感到驚訝。

cues.en: On the other hand, something that has a probability of 0.5 has a lot of entropy.
cues.zh: 另一方面，機率為 0.5 的事情，熵就很高。

cues.en: So here you can think about flipping a coin.
cues.zh: 可以想像擲硬幣。

cues.en: The coin has an equal chance of landing on heads or tails, and therefore the outcome is more variable.
cues.zh: 硬幣出現正面或反面的機率相同，因此結果較具變化性。

cues.en: Now, in the context of information theory that probability has a high entropy.
cues.zh: 在資訊理論的脈絡下，這個機率具有高熵。

cues.en: So you can also think of the entropy as being like the predictability of a system.
cues.zh: 所以也可以把熵，想成系統的可預測性。

cues.en: So if you can accurately predict a particular outcome then the entropy will be low.
cues.zh: 如果可以準確預測某個結果，熵就低；

cues.en: But if you cannot predict an outcome then the entropy is higher.
cues.zh: 如果無法預測結果，熵就比較高。

cues.en: Now these are all somewhat vague and imprecise statements.
cues.zh: 這些說法都有些模糊、不精確。

cues.en: And I'll show you the formula on the next slide.
cues.zh: 下一張投影片會展示公式。

cues.en: But I do want to lighten the mood a little bit after the previous slide, and say that entropy in information
cues.zh: 不過，經過上一張投影片，我想稍微輕鬆一下：資訊理論中的熵

cues.en: theory states that everything and everyone is great and happy, and we all like being surprised because surprises convey more Information.
cues.zh: 表示，一切、每個人都很棒很快樂，而且大家都喜歡驚喜，因為驚喜帶來更多資訊。

cues.en: Okay, let's do some math.
cues.zh: 好，來做點數學。

cues.en: Here is the formula for entropy in information theory.
cues.zh: 這是資訊理論中熵的公式，

cues.en: It's often indicated using a capital H.
cues.zh: 經常用大寫 H 表示。

cues.en: The formula itself is pretty straightforward.
cues.zh: 公式本身相當直接。

cues.en: You need to know the probability of certain events taking place or being observed.
cues.zh: 需要知道某些事件發生，或被觀察到的機率，

cues.en: And then you simply multiply the probability by the log of the probability.
cues.zh: 然後將機率乘以該機率的對數，

cues.en: And then you sum up over all of the possible data categories.
cues.zh: 再對所有可能的資料類別加總，

cues.en: So that would be n data categories.
cues.zh: 也就是 n 個資料類別。

cues.en: And then you have your entropy.
cues.zh: 這樣就得到熵。

cues.en: Now because probabilities are all between 0 and 1 the log of those probabilities will be negative.
cues.zh: 因為機率都介於 0 和 1 之間，其對數會是負值，

cues.en: And so the sum will necessarily be negative.
cues.zh: 因此總和必然為負。

cues.en: Therefore we add a negative sign out front just so that entropy ends up being positive.
cues.zh: 所以在前面加上負號，讓熵最後變成正值，

cues.en: And that just makes the interpretation a little bit easier.
cues.zh: 解讀起來也比較容易。

cues.en: You can also see that there is a potential problem with this formula when the probability is zero.
cues.zh: 另外可以看到，機率為零時，這個公式可能有問題。

cues.en: So the log of zero is not a finite number.
cues.zh: 零的對數不是有限數，

cues.en: So we can have numerical problems with this calculation.
cues.zh: 因此計算可能出現數值問題。

cues.en: In practice there are a few ways to deal with this.
cues.zh: 實務上有幾種處理方式。

cues.en: One way is to ignore from the analysis any probabilities that are exactly zero.
cues.zh: 一種是從分析中忽略所有恰好為零的機率。

cues.en: And another option is to add a very tiny number inside the log.
cues.zh: 另一種是在對數裡面加上一個非常微小的數字。

cues.en: Now, that number would be so small that it doesn't really impact the analysis for non-zero probabilities.
cues.zh: 這個數字小到不會真正影響非零機率的分析。

cues.en: And if the probability is zero, then the log of that tiny number will be some really large negative number.
cues.zh: 如果機率為零，那個微小數字的對數，就會是一個很大的負數，

cues.en: But then it gets multiplied by the probability out here, which is still zero.
cues.zh: 但接著會乘上外面的機率，而機率仍然是零。

cues.en: Anyway, I'll show you some of these Approaches for numerical stability when I switch to code.
cues.zh: 切換到程式碼後，我會示範其中一些維持數值穩定的方法。

cues.en: Now, one difficulty of using entropy is that this formula is really designed for categorical events,
cues.zh: 使用熵有個困難，這個公式其實是為類別事件設計的，

cues.en: like a coin landing on heads or tails, or a token index, or a grammatical category like noun or verb or adjective.
cues.zh: 例如硬幣落在正面或反面、token 索引，或名詞、動詞、形容詞等語法類別。

cues.en: But we are going to use entropy and mutual information on activation values, which are continuous numbers.
cues.zh: 但我們要對活化值使用熵與互資訊，而活化值是連續數值。

cues.en: So that causes some headaches.
cues.zh: 所以這會造成一些麻煩。

cues.en: And the solution is to use histograms to approximate probabilities.
cues.zh: 解法是使用直方圖，近似機率。

cues.en: And unfortunately that also can lead to some headaches because it means that we need to choose the number of bins and the method of binning the data.
cues.zh: 不幸的是，這也可能造成麻煩，因為必須選擇分箱數量，以及將資料分箱的方法。

cues.en: And these parameter choices can impact the entropy estimation.
cues.zh: 這些參數選擇，可能影響熵的估計。

cues.en: I'll talk about this in more detail in code.
cues.zh: 程式部分會再詳細說明。

cues.en: Although to be honest, a really detailed discussion of this is more for a course on statistics or machine learning.
cues.zh: 不過老實說，要真正詳細討論，比較適合放在統計或機器學習課程。

cues.en: So I'm not going to get into a ton of detail about it here.
cues.zh: 所以這裡不會深入太多細節。

cues.en: Anyway, the upshot of all this math is that when the data set has a lot of variability, then entropy
cues.zh: 總之，這些數學的結論是，資料集的變異很多時，熵

cues.en: is higher.
cues.zh: 就比較高。

cues.en: And the flip side of that interpretation is that when entropy is low, it means that the data has a lot of redundancies.
cues.zh: 反過來說，熵低就表示資料有很多冗餘，

cues.en: That means the data are highly predictable.
cues.zh: 也就是資料高度可預測。

cues.en: In other words, entropy is a measure of the variability of the data.
cues.zh: 換句話說，熵衡量的是資料的變異程度。

cues.en: But you're already familiar with another quantification of variability, which is the standard deviation or variance.
cues.zh: 但你已經熟悉另一種量化變異程度的方式，也就是標準差或變異數。

cues.en: So how does entropy relate to variance.
cues.zh: 所以熵與變異數有什麼關係？

cues.en: Well, the short version of the story is that variance is a linear measure of variability, whereas entropy is a nonlinear measure.
cues.zh: 簡單來說，變異數是線性的變異程度指標，而熵是非線性指標。

cues.en: So entropy also doesn't really make assumptions about the distribution of the data, whereas variance is based on interpreting the mean.
cues.zh: 熵也不太對資料分布做假設，變異數則是以解讀平均數為基礎。

cues.en: And so variance and also standard deviation are mainly interpretable or mainly suitable for data that
cues.zh: 因此，變異數與標準差，主要適合用於至少有些

cues.en: are at least somewhat normally distributed, and that is not the case for entropy with entropy.
cues.zh: 接近常態分布的資料，也主要在那種情況下才容易解讀；熵則不同。

cues.en: You can have any data distribution that happens to be observed.
cues.zh: 熵可以處理實際觀察到的任何資料分布。

cues.en: In the next video, I'm going to talk more about the relationship between mutual information and covariance.
cues.zh: 下一支影片會進一步討論互資訊與共變異數的關係，

cues.en: So I'll also get back to this discussion in later videos.
cues.zh: 因此後面幾支影片也會再回到這個討論。

cues.en: So let's now talk about mutual information.
cues.zh: 現在來談互資訊。

cues.en: If you think of this Venn diagram as the entropy in variable x and this is the entropy in variable y.
cues.zh: 把這個文氏圖想成變數 x 的熵，這個則是變數 y 的熵，

cues.en: Then where they overlap over here.
cues.zh: 那麼它們在這裡重疊的部分，

cues.en: That is the mutual information.
cues.zh: 就是互資訊。

cues.en: I will show two formulas for calculating mutual information on the following slide.
cues.zh: 下一張投影片會展示兩個計算互資訊的公式。

cues.en: But essentially the idea is that mutual information is designed to quantify how much you can know about one variable if you measure another variable.
cues.zh: 但基本概念是，互資訊用來量化，測量某個變數後，能知道另一個變數多少資訊。

cues.en: And we can think about two extremes.
cues.zh: 可以想像兩個極端。

cues.en: Let's say you measure the amount of hydrogen in different stars in the Milky Way galaxy.
cues.zh: 假設測量銀河系不同恆星中的氫含量，

cues.en: And you also measured the price of Bitcoin in the past ten years.
cues.zh: 同時測量過去十年比特幣的價格。

cues.en: Those two variables have literally nothing whatsoever to do with each other.
cues.zh: 這兩個變數，根本完全沒有任何關係，

cues.en: And so the mutual information between them would be zero.
cues.zh: 所以它們之間的互資訊會是零。

cues.en: On the other hand, let's say you measure the price of Bitcoin and the price of Ethereum over the past ten years.
cues.zh: 另一方面，假設測量過去十年，比特幣與以太幣的價格。

cues.en: Now, those two variables are closely related to each other.
cues.zh: 這兩個變數彼此密切相關。

cues.en: They're not identical, but it certainly is the case that knowing the price of Ethereum gives you some indication of the price of Bitcoin.
cues.zh: 它們並不相同，但確實知道以太幣價格，就能對比特幣價格有些概念。

cues.en: So the mutual information between those two variables would be significantly larger than zero.
cues.zh: 所以這兩個變數之間的互資訊，會明顯大於零。

cues.en: And what exactly could you say about the price of Bitcoin if you knew the price of Ethereum using mutual information?
cues.zh: 那麼，如果知道以太幣價格，用互資訊究竟能對比特幣價格說出什麼？

cues.en: Well here mutual information is not so super duper helpful.
cues.zh: 在這裡，互資訊就沒有那麼有幫助了。

cues.en: If you want to make an actual prediction about the value of one variable given the value of another variable.
cues.zh: 如果想根據某個變數的值，真正預測另一個變數的值，

cues.en: Then mutual information is just not the proper analysis.
cues.zh: 互資訊就不是適當的分析。

cues.en: So mutual information tells you about the overlap of predictability of one variable and another, but
cues.zh: 互資訊告訴你，一個變數與另一個變數的可預測性重疊多少，

cues.en: it does not tell you the exact values of one variable, given what you know about another variable.
cues.zh: 但不會告訴你，已知一個變數時，另一個變數的精確數值。

cues.en: Mutual information is often indicated using the capital letter I.
cues.zh: 互資訊經常用大寫 I 表示。

cues.en: So here you see two different but equivalent formulas for mutual information.
cues.zh: 這裡是兩個不同，但等價的互資訊公式。

cues.en: Now mutual information is always calculated between two variables.
cues.zh: 互資訊永遠是在兩個變數之間計算，

cues.en: It's a bivariate measure of statistical dependency.
cues.zh: 是統計相依性的雙變量指標。

cues.en: So x and y would be two different variables.
cues.zh: x 與 y 就是兩個不同變數，

cues.en: Let's say for example two different neurons in an MLP transformer Subblock.
cues.zh: 例如 Transformer 的 MLP 子區塊中的兩個不同神經元。

cues.en: Now this first formula here looks an awful lot like entropy, except that the joint probability of x
cues.zh: 第一個公式看起來非常像熵，只是 x

cues.en: and Y is normalized by the individual probabilities.
cues.zh: 與 y 的聯合機率，除以它們各自的機率作正規化。

cues.en: This second formula here is more similar to the Venn diagram that I showed in the previous slide, which you also see here.
cues.zh: 第二個公式，比較像上一張投影片的文氏圖，這裡也可以看到。

cues.en: So in other words, you add up the entropies of each of the two variables individually, and then you subtract off what you can learn about the two of them together.
cues.zh: 換句話說，將兩個變數各自的熵相加，再減去同時觀察兩者能得知的資訊。

cues.en: Now, it might initially seem strange that we are adding the individual entropies and then subtracting
cues.zh: 一開始可能覺得，將各自的熵相加，再減去

cues.en: off the joint entropy, but remember that entropy is defined using a minus sign.
cues.zh: 聯合熵很奇怪，但記住，熵的定義本來就有負號。

cues.en: So you can actually think about inverting these signs to say that it's the joint entropy minus the entropies of the two individual variables.
cues.zh: 所以也可以想成，將這些正負號反轉，變成聯合熵減去兩個個別變數的熵。

cues.en: By the way, you might have noticed that the formula I used for entropy had a log two base in a previous slide, whereas here I'm using the natural log.
cues.zh: 順帶一提，你可能注意到，前面投影片的熵公式使用以 2 為底的對數，這裡卻用自然對數。

cues.en: Now in practice you would consistently use one or the other.
cues.zh: 實際使用時，應該一致採用其中一種，

cues.en: So either log base two or the natural log, but the base of the logarithm doesn't actually matter in most applications of mutual information.
cues.zh: 也就是以 2 為底，或自然對數。但在互資訊的大多數應用中，對數底數其實不重要。

cues.en: It does change the units of the results, for example bits versus nats.
cues.zh: 它確實會改變結果的單位，例如 bit 與 nat，

cues.en: In this case, but that doesn't change the relative mutual information between different variables or different conditions.
cues.zh: 但不會改變不同變數或不同條件之間的相對互資訊。

cues.en: I would also like to point out that all of these formulas for entropy and mutual information are not based on the data themselves.
cues.zh: 也想指出，這些熵與互資訊公式，全部都不是直接基於資料本身，

cues.en: They're based on the probabilities of the data values or the data bins.
cues.zh: 而是基於資料值或資料分箱的機率。

cues.en: And that means that the scale of the data has no impact on mutual information.
cues.zh: 這表示，資料尺度不會影響互資訊。

cues.en: So for example, if you would multiply the data values by a billion, that literally has no impact on the mutual information value.
cues.zh: 例如，將資料值乘以十億，對互資訊的數值完全沒有影響。

cues.en: And I mentioned that as a bit of a segue to comparing mutual information to covariance, which you will learn about in the next video.
cues.zh: 提到這點，是為了銜接下一支影片要學的互資訊與共變異數比較。

cues.en: And it will also be relevant a couple of videos thereafter.
cues.zh: 再後面幾支影片，也會與此有關。

cues.en: Anyway, as I mentioned a few slides ago, this formula is pretty straightforward when you have discrete categories.
cues.zh: 總之，幾張投影片前提過，如果是離散類別，這個公式相當直接。

cues.en: But we are working with continuous activation numbers.
cues.zh: 但我們處理的是連續活化數值，

cues.en: So floating point numbers.
cues.zh: 也就是浮點數。

cues.en: And so all of these calculations have to be based on estimating probabilities using histograms and joint histograms.
cues.zh: 所以這些計算，都必須利用直方圖與聯合直方圖估計機率。

cues.en: And that leads me to the Python demo.
cues.zh: 這就帶到 Python 示範。

cues.en: The purpose of the Python demo is to show you the basics of implementing entropy and mutual information.
cues.zh: Python 示範的目的，是介紹實作熵與互資訊的基礎。

cues.en: I will introduce some additional nuances to mutual information over the next several videos.
cues.zh: 接下來幾支影片，還會介紹互資訊更多細節。

cues.en: So to start with I'm going to generate some bivariate data that has a statistical dependency built in.
cues.zh: 首先會產生一組雙變量資料，並刻意讓它們有統計相依性，

cues.en: And that's what you see here.
cues.zh: 就是這裡看到的。

cues.en: Now it's just two arbitrary variables, and it's clear that they are correlated.
cues.zh: 它們只是兩個任意變數，但明顯具有相關。
